newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London drift off, led by HSBC.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London drift off, led by HSBC.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London were largely inactive on Monday, but tracking the FTSE lower after the Hong Kong market closed at a new record high.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was down 15.22 points at 12,544.18 by 1510 GMT.
"We've been stuck in a tight 20-point trading range," said one dealer. "We're looking tired and just drifting off."
HSBC Holdings, the bell-wether stock, came under pressure, dragging the rest of the market with it, dealers said.
The shares were trading at HK$158.975 in London, after closing in Hong Kong at HK$159.500.

In Hong Kong on Monday, the Hang Seng index rose 30.13 points to 12,559.40, a record closing high, but traders said the U.S. presidential election, which kicks off on Tuesday, is likely to take centre stage.
"The market reached an all time high and other markets are looking a bit toppy, so who wants to commit new money at the moment?" one said.
